h: From the Broken Tablets to the Light of Redemption

p: מִן שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז עַד תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב
from the seventeenth of Tammuz to the ninth of Av:
the first and last days always fall
on the day of the week on which falls
the first day of Pesach, as is known.
that on the night of the first day of Pesach,
Yisrael were then chosen by Hashem as a people,
"And I will take you to Me as a people."
And the main purpose of the Exodus from Egypt
"When you bring the people out of Egypt,
And this is what it says:
in the aspect of a bride,
throughout the book of Shir HaShirim.
and then the marriage was annulled
"Better that she be judged as an unmarried woman, etc.";
and on the ninth of Av the Temple was destroyed,
the first time and the second,
so that through it they would merit
עַל שְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פז, א)
About the breaking of the Tablets they said (Shabbos 87a):
for through the breaking of the Tablets
they merited the light of the Oral Torah,
in the second Tablets I will give you
And on the ninth of Av
on the pasuk "For the comforter is far from me");
and the destruction of the Temple was
a preparation for the building of the Third,
which will be by the hands of Heaven
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ל, סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
(as Rashi wrote, Rosh Hashanah, end of 30a);
and then there will be a complete redemption,
after which there will be no exile,
"All the songs are in the feminine form, etc.,
except for that of the future,
after which there is no suffering or subjugation."
And in the three of retribution
and to merit the three expressions
that were said regarding the redemption from Egypt:
"And I will bring out, and I will rescue, and I will redeem" (Shemos 6:6);
from the three roots of the kelipos,
the kelipah of Esav and Yishmael,
שֶׁכּוֹלְלִין ע׳ קְלִיפּוֹת שֶׁל ע׳ אוּמּוֹת
which include the seventy kelipos of the seventy nations,
thirty-five from the right and thirty-five from the left
which is the beginning of the kelipah,
"Amalek was the first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:20),
and it is the Da'as of the kelipah.
And afterward on the ninth of Av we merit
that there be "And I will take you to Me as a people,
and I will be your God."
And likewise the four cups of Pesach
correspond to the four expressions of redemption
שֶׁחָל תָּמִיד הַשְּׁנֵי יָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
that the two days mentioned above always fall
on the day on which the first day of Pesach falls.
